marking_scheme.q1: Osmosis (2): movement of water (1) across a partially permeable membrane from high to low water concentration / down a water potential gradient (1). Diffusion (2): net movement of particles (1) from high to low concentration / down a concentration gradient (1).
marking_scheme.q2: (a, 4): substrate binds to the enzyme's active site (1); the active site is not a rigid lock, it changes shape / moulds around the substrate (1); this strains bonds or holds substrates together so reaction is more likely (1); products released, enzyme unchanged and reusable (1). (b, 4): high temperature breaks the bonds holding the enzyme's shape (1); active site shape changes / enzyme denatures (1); substrate no longer fits (1); reaction rate falls (1).
marking_scheme.q3: Any two of (2 marks each): plant cells have a cell wall, animal cells do not; plant cells have chloroplasts, animal cells do not; plant cells have a large permanent vacuole, animal cells have small vacuoles or none. Max 4.
marking_scheme.q4: No nucleus leaves more room for haemoglobin (2); so each cell can carry more oxygen (1); small flexible / biconcave shape helps squeeze through capillaries (1).

questions.prompt: Enzymes. (a) Describe the induced-fit model of enzyme action. (b) Explain why the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction falls at high temperatures.
State any two differences between plant and animal cells.
Explain why mature red blood cells have no nucleus.

reference_note: Accept phonetic spelling. For q3, mark only the first two differences stated and ignore the rest.
title: BIO101 class test 1: cells and enzymes
